utterances.text: Mr. Zaric was not arrested, he voluntarily surrendered and I would like to clarify that. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry, I didn't -- I have no quarrel with that proposition. That was my mistake. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just one other question on the Crisis Staff: Do you know when it was formed?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I can jog your memory and tell me if this has that effect. In the gazette that I showed you earlier, Exhibit P124, there was a preamble written by Mitar Mitrovic. In that preamble, he says that the Crisis Staff was formed on the 15th of April, 15th of April, in a place called St. Sava's hall. Having heard that, does it jog your memory? Do you now remember and is he correct? If not, say so.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, and I cannot testify about things that I don't have precise information about. The only thing I know is that when I saw one of those people for the first time from the Crisis Staff that we were talking about was on the 19th of April in Pik, the agricultural combine, Pik, and I saw them there for the first time but there were some other people there also, not only the ones we talked about, there were also deputies, people were coming and going, and I think that it was only then that the Crisis Staff started to function in some kind of form.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I've got to know so that I can make the decision, Mr. Ninkovic. What is your position? Let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one correction for the transcript. Page 45, line 7, I heard the witness say that he saw some of those people and in the translation, in English, it says that he saw them, but he said that he saw some of those people on the 19th. That's what I heard in the original language. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ninkovic, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have that confirmed by the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, some of those people. That's what I said. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your -- are you saying that you just -- you just don't know when the Crisis Staff was formed and so it could be on the 15th, that is at some point before the 16th and 17th of April? Or are you saying, no, it is far more likely that it was formed after the 16th and 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am close to this last stance of yours so that it was on the 19th that it started to function. I don't know whether this was a spontaneous meeting and they decided to then continue working in sessions or whether somebody convened it. That's something that I cannot testify about, but I did see at that place some of those people that we talked about. I saw some deputies of the municipal assembly of Samac. I also saw Mirko Lukic from the executive board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's see if we can get through this topic as quickly as we can. I don't want to dwell upon it but can the witness be shown P124, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Di Fazio in your questions, last two questions, you were asking Mr. Ninkovic when the Crisis Staff was formed, but in Mr. Ninkovic's answers in translation, for example, page 46, line 6, he is talking about when it started to function. Now it strikes me that those two could be the same, formed and functioning on the same date, or it could be different, formed on one date starting to function on another. MR. DI FAZIO: I take Your Honour's point and I will clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You probably understood Her Honour's distinction. Is it possible that the Crisis Staff was formed at an earlier point in time, before the 15th and 16th but only really got going with its business after that date?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that I have about that, or the knowledge that I have, is that the Crisis Staff started to function after the beginning of the war, but I don't have knowledge about it being formed before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now that you have P124 before you, let me just draw your attention to a couple of matters. First of all, the preamble at the very beginning of the document, Mitar Mitrovic's preamble, secretary of the municipal assembly, he says, towards the end of that preamble, and it's a separate paragraph, "The Crisis Staff was formed in the St. Sava hall of the church of the holy mother in Obudovac on the 15th of April, 1992." Do you see that? So he's quite specific, he's got a date, he's got a place. He's got a town. Quite specific information. Is he -- have you any reason to doubt that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not disputing that. It says so here quite decisively but that is not my testimony. I don't have any knowledge about that but I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know as much about it as you do on the basis of the text. MR. DI FAZIO: All right. Thank you very much. I've finished with that document for the time being, and if Mr. Usher pleases, I think -- yes, I've finished with that document and any other documents that are there with the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The simple, broad situation is this, in terms of the life of the institutions in Bosanski Samac: On the 15th of April, 1992, the municipality of Bosanski Samac existed, the municipality of Bosanski Samac that had existed for many years, and on the 17th, it no longer did. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I wish to say is that the local assembly fell apart, which was based on the will of the voters. So this assembly fell apart along national lines and it could not be put back together again. So we can talk about the breakdown of power in the municipality of Bosanski Samac and we can also talk about the same type of breaking up of power all over Bosnia and Herzegovina. At the same time we can talk about the process of constructing state organs of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the territory of Bosanski Samac, the municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree, I think, at least, that the assembly of the Bosanski Samac municipality did not dissolve itself?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such document that it was being dissolved, but it could not be convened. There was no forum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's because on the 17th, the town was crawling with Serb forces and Serb paramilitaries, isn't it? And its members and Croats and Muslims were being arrested?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, in the period before the 17th of April, several months before, there was no meeting of the municipal assembly, the one that was elected in 1990 in the first free elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at the issue by reference to language that was used at the time. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P89?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just acquaint yourself with that. Right. Paragraph 2, or perhaps sorry, paragraph 1, it simply establishes a state of emergency, this is on the 19th of April, and then in the next paragraph, at the stroke of a pen, out go the bodies and institutions of Bosanski Samac municipality, I quote, "They shall cease to operate in their current mandate." And then you have the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac taking up their functions. You couldn't want for a clearer, more emphatic document, could you? It makes the situation abundantly clear, the old municipality ceases to exist and the new one takes over. That's -- and in fact, that represents reality, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with you, and here is why. First of all, item 1, state of emergency is being introduced into in the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac in view of the fact that war had already begun, that's why we had the state of emergency so in a way it was already verified. There was a situation of war in the territory of that municipality. So it is only a verification here of what we already have on the ground. This is how I experience article 1 or paragraph 1 of this decision. If you look at paragraph 2 of this decision, I interpret it as meaning that new coordination was required in the sense of functioning of normal life in the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: New coordination? How do you get new coordination out of the words "shall cease to operate in their current mandate and the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality shall take up their functions, rights and obligations"? That's not new coordination. That is a takeover, pure and simple, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your interpretation does not -- is not in accordance with the factual situation. We can say that in the territory of the municipality, you had the municipal authorities, the parliamentary authorities, and the executive authorities. The assembly was not able to convene for several months, nor could the executive board. So who was this power taken from, if these organs already did not exist in the municipality, the assembly didn't exist or the executive board. This is an effort to introduce -- to approach the constituting of the organs of power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, the fact -- you say that the old municipality that had existed, the old assembly, hadn't been able to function for months. And is it your position that this was widely known and everyone understood this in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was known in the whole territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina that there was a crisis in the functioning of the organs of power at the level of the republic and at the municipal level also, so this was well known. It was discussed every day on the television, in the newspapers, over the radio, so there was a crisis of authority, of power, in Bosnia and Herzegovina. There were opposing stances by the national communities of that republic, on very key questions, key issues, and this disunity was transferred from the top, from the President through the republican assembly, down to the municipalities. All the institutions of power in Bosnia and Herzegovina were falling apart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So a vacuum of power had existed and the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac stepped in because of that vacuum of power. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite like that. The JNA thwarted an attack on Samac on the 17th and it was necessary then to start to coordinate the issues from the civilian domain and this is what the Crisis Staff took upon itself, until the other organs of power, the ministries, were set up, and this was later confirmed by things that happened, by documents, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the old municipality of Bosanski Samac, the old assembly, was moribund, had ceased to effectively function and there was a vacuum of power and it was because of that or partially because of that, that the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac was set up, why didn't paragraph 2 say that? Perhaps in different words but why did it not convey that meaning?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that instead of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, it should be the municipality of Bosanski Samac? Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't paragraph 2 say that in view of the fact that the old municipality of Bosanski Samac was moribund, no longer functioning, no longer able to function, the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac shall step in and take up its functions? It doesn't say that. It says they shall cease to operate. It's very clear when you read it.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had already ceased operation, but I will agree with you that the terms used are not as precise as they could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The result was that the Croatian and Muslim people, people of Muslim and Croatian ethnicity living in Bosanski Samac and in the municipality were effectively stripped of any political representation following the events of the 15th -- sorry, the 16th and 17th. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Dayton Accords stated things as it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no, I'm not asking you about the Dayton Accords. I'm not asking you about that. I'm asking you about 1992 and the early part of 1993. The result was, following the events of the 16th and 17th, that the Croatian and Muslim people who had lived or -- and who lived in the town of Bosanski Samac and the municipality were stripped of any representation, any political representation. If you wish, I can take you to the gazettes and the new statutes and show you the language and I'll do that if necessary but I can save time and simply put that proposition to you.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood you. At that point, new elections would be necessary, in view of the fact that there was a war going on, elections were not possible. So this situation lasted until the signing of the Dayton peace accords. This is why I mentioned the Dayton peace accords.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we will be a little more specific. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown P124, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Paragraph 1 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio sorry to interrupt you, on the transcript I can see Exhibit P124 that was the exhibit provided to the witness, is that the correct exhibit. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you, P124, the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the first paragraph, the first decision following Mr. Mitrovic's preamble. "Decision to establish an Assembly of the Serbian People of the municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under formation." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go straight to Article 5, please. Now, there it is in black and white, very clear, "The assembly is to consist of deputies of the Serbian Democratic Party, various places, and other deputies of Serbian ethnicity." No mention of Muslims or Croats. Now, the effect of that is very, very simple and very, very plain, isn't it? That's the end of political representation for Croats and Muslims, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it states in Article 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure does.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you read it. But in my opinion, this should be linked to the referendum about the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was carried out --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Frankly, I'm not asking you for your opinion. I'm simply asking you what the effect of this is in black and white. Article 5 is very, very clear. There is no reference to any referendum. It's very simple. The assembly is only going to be SDS members and other deputies of Serb ethnicity. That's the group that is going to compose the new assembly. Nothing about Croats and nothing about Muslims. Now, surely, surely you have to agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that that is what it states here, if you're looking for me to comment on it, yes, I will do that, and if you wish me to read Article 5, I will do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. Thank you. And the interests of the Serbian people only are further entrenched in Article 6, because it then says that the assemblies got to recognise all federal regulations and so on as long as they don't infringe upon the interests of the Serbian people. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to give you my comment for those very reasons, but you didn't permit me to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If you -- if your position is that your comment will help explain these Article 5 and 6, please go ahead and provide us with your comment.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The referendum that was carried out in the autumn of 1992 was against the will of the Serb people, that was one of the constituent peoples of the BH. The constitution of BH stipulated unequivocally that major decisions had to be reached by way of consensus of the three peoples. Since this referendum violated the elementary basic right of the Serbs, that is to say it violated the constitution, since the Serbs believe that they should remain within the federal state and in Article 6, that is linked to that. While the Muslims and the Croats wanted the B and H to be outside Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you for the history of events in 1991 and 1992. Nor the reasons why this gazette -- sorry, this statute was adopted in the form that it is, that it is in. I'm simply asking you this: The effect of Article 5 and 6 was to disenfranchise Croats and Muslims who lived in the municipality. That's undeniable, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we were to take things out of a general context, then there would be some elements of that which you have been referring to, but taking things out of a general context and out of a general situation on the ground would not be right, and as such, it cannot be decisive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Individual, isolated incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, I cut you off. I didn't mean to do that. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually I disagree with your intention. To take individual things out of a general context and then you want me to confirm that to have been the dominant policy, that is to say the approach of the authorities in the municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: With the witness be shown P125, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the meantime Your Honour it's page 54, line 10, there is a some reference to the referendum which was carried out in the autumn of 1992. Obviously, it's maybe a mistake in the transcript. The referendum was not in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, can that be corrected? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the sake of the record, you meant 1991, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Quick look at P125. Now, you have it there. This is the Statute. Now this time I can tell you that you'll find the portion that I'm interested in at page 4 of the B/C/S -- of the B/C/S. The Statute of the municipality, item 1, municipality.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said page 4?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, page 4 of the B/C/S version. And it talks about the municipality, Article 1.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rights and responsibilities of the municipality? Talking about the Statute of the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I believe it says this: "Article 1, Samac municipality shall be a municipality of the Serbian people and other citizens living there." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is preference -- why are the Serbian people mentioned in particular? Why doesn't it just refer to Serbian -- sorry to people who are living there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the approach.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Perhaps more relevantly I should direct your attention to Article 51 and that's on page 9 of the B/C/S. That sets out membership of the municipal assembly. Do you see that? That says that the Samac municipal assembly is to consist of SDS members.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm following you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And other members of other parties who were Serbs. Now the effect of that is disenfranchisement of Croats and Muslims, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the expression you used is too strong, that there would be disenfranchisement. No. Now, again what did you ask me? My answer is related to the Dayton Accords again, the Dayton peace agreement. It ratified the disintegration of Bosnia-Herzegovina as it was in the constitution of 1991, so it verified that this state no longer existed and it also verified a new Bosnia-Herzegovina, new Dayton Bosnia-Herzegovina, with new constitutional solutions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me perhaps approach it from the point of view of a concrete example. If -- the municipal assembly started operating again in early 1993, right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff had been and gone and the same for the War Presidency and now it was the Serbian municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the municipal assembly, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if for whatever reason a member of that assembly had to be replaced, a Croat or a Muslim simply couldn't stand for election, simply couldn't seek office, could they, because they are not Serb? It's as simple as that. That's the effect of those provisions, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not the way it was, and now I'll tell you why. First of all, all these councilmen were elected in the election in 1991 so none of them were illegitimate. All of them were legitimately, legally elected at the first free elections. However the territorial organisation was different of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Ninkovic, but I thought your earlier testimony was that the preexisting structures in the municipality were no longer in operative effect, and I believe the document Mr. Di Fazio showed you was talking about such ceasing to exist. So I'm just a little uncertain what the relevance of the election of these people in the first free elections has to do with the newly formed assembly that we are talking about now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You did not understand me, Judge Williams. I am talking about the councilmen, the assemblymen. I said they were legitimate because they were elected in the first elections in 1990. So it's not that there were some elections that were held after that. So these assemblymen were legitimate. However, the assemblies where they were before the war, where they worked before the war, these assemblies no longer functioned. New assemblies were created. But out of the ranks of the assemblymen that were elected in 1990. Did I manage to make things clearer now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. I think so. But just one follow-up question. But out of -- you say out of the ranks of the assemblymen that were elected in 1990, but we are talking strictly of assemblymen or women, I presume, of Serb ethnicity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, but also assemblymen of Croat ethnicity functioned in Odzak or in Orasje or in the municipality of Domaljevac, a new municipality, because the area was recomposed, the area of the municipalities, and this was done along ethnic lines but that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that the Serb members of the Serbian municipality that started operating in early 1993 had been elected earlier, and I understand that they were members of the old municipality of Bosanski Samac. I've got no problem in understanding that. What I'm putting to you is this: The result of all of those provisions that I showed you in the gazettes, P124 and P126, is that following the establishment of the Serbian Assembly of -- municipal assembly of Bosanski Samac, Croats and Muslims could no longer be representatives of people, whatever people, in this assembly because it was an exclusive club, it was confined to Serbs. Now, is that -- that's as clear as I can put it. Now, do you agree or not? You don't have to agree with me but just let me know your position.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You see, every elected assemblymen, elected in the free elections, is independent. That is to say he cannot be replaced, because he has behind him the legitimacy of direct elections. It is his own free will where he is going to represent his voters. If an assemblyman of the municipal assembly of Bosanski Samac decided later to represent his voters in the newly established municipality of Domaljevac, a Croat municipality, that is his own free will. If an assemblyman who was a Serb decided to represent his voters in the Serb Municipality of Bosanski Samac, again that is a matter of his own will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that in this assembly, there weren't any assemblymen who had not been elected in the free elections in 1990. That is to say that all of them had the legitimacy of the free elections behind them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except that their Croat and Muslim counterparts, they were no longer carrying out their functions as political representatives of their people who had lived in Bosanski Samac and the municipality of Bosanski Samac. That's the case, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know now what the situation was in 1993, when the assembly started working, how many assemblymen of other ethnic backgrounds there were in Samac. I cannot really give you that kind of a cross section now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I hadn't asked for numbers but I'll withdraw that. Let's turn to another topic on representation. Do you agree that the villages and small communities that existed within the municipality of Bosanski Samac prior to -- prior to the war, used to have a form of representation on the local village Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I beg your pardon. Would you please repeat your question? Because I could not focus for a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just compose yourself and I'll rephrase my question so you can understand clearly. What I'm -- what I'm asking you is this: Before the war, Croats and Serbs who lived in small villages within the municipality of Bosanski Samac had a form of representation because there existed small, local village crisis staffs, right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. If you mean the councils of local communes, then yes, the councils of local communes. Those were the regular authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this lowest level, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I can save time and ask you simply to look at P91 and P92. And while we are waiting for that to be delivered to you, there is no doubt, is there, that some villages in Bosanski Samac, in the municipality, were exclusively Croat villages? That is inhabited mainly by Croats and some villages were inhabited mainly by Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So look at P91, first of all.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the order related to the ban of political parties?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apologies. I apologise to the Chamber and I apologise to the witness, and to the usher. I've asked for the wrong documents to be placed before him. I in fact need P106 and P107. I apologise for that confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. On your request, Mr. Di Fazio, for more time, the Trial Chamber conferred and we decided that we will give you 20 minutes more. MR. DI FAZIO: May I just have a chance to confer with my colleague, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It is 20 minutes after the break. After we've taken our break. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. 20 minutes after the break. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just have a quick look at 106, please. I don't want to spend too much time on this but the effect of this is the local communes are dissolved and the Crisis Staff appoints its own people in those local, small village communes, right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This decision pertains to that subject. That is to say what you said just now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The effect of that, therefore, is that any representation that Croats in Croat villages in the municipality of Bosanski Samac might have had through their village Crisis Staff, was gone. That was the end of that. And the Crisis Staff of which Dr. Blagoje Simic was president, now had control even at that level. That's the effect of it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the way it should be interpreted. This is a narrow interpretation. One has to look at Article 3 where it says that a special decision would regulate the position of the local commune. So the motive of this decision is not for the Croats or the Muslims or rather for the Croats to be thrown out of the authorities in the local communes. There is probably some other motive behind this decision. Perhaps some shortcomings were noted in the work of these local communes. I would not agree that this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is the way you are asking the questions because now the witness is just speculating. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I'm not inviting him to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He's a fact witness so the questions should be to elicit evidence of facts, not what was intended, what was the motive. MR. DI FAZIO: No, no, I don't want the motive. I want the effect of this document and that's the question, with respect, Your Honour, I asked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not asking you what the reason behind this was. I'm suggesting to you that the simple effect of this document is that even at village level, even at village level, any representation of the people on the local village Crisis Staff is ended and the Crisis Staff, the Crisis Staff that was in Bosanski Samac, the town, has placed its people in those positions. So it controls not just the town but the whole municipality, village by village, commune by commune.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand what you're after, that total authority was taken over by the Crisis Staff, that they took control from the lowest level upwards and that that is what this decision says. I told you already that this is a very narrow interpretation and I cannot agree with it. I would rather put it this way: That the intention involved here is to organise these local communes in a clearer way. It was probably noted that there were some shortcomings in their work, so better organisation and coordination were aimed at in order to have this work carried out in a better way on the ground. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, may I ask what time you intend to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have a break at 1745. This is one and a half hours, one and a half hours, and then you have a 20 minutes break. MR. DI FAZIO: I have finished this with this particular topic. I'm about to embark on the next topic. Now, I'd like an opportunity if I may to confer with my colleague, Mr. Weiner, regarding the remainder of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you want us to take the break now. MR. DI FAZIO: Would it matter if we took the break, it's only a matter of two or three minutes and that will help me devise the next 20 minutes and I'd like to do that with my colleague if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will take the break now and continue our proceedings at 1805.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Can the witness be shown Exhibit P72?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw this document earlier this afternoon. I would just like to highlight a number of the more important features of it, Witness. Firstly, this is the document that orders the transformation of Crisis Staffs into War Presidencies, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is an example, is it not, of state or republican institutions interfering or perhaps interfering is not the right word, affecting municipal level institutions?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you are trying to say with that. The jurisdictions of certain institutions are well known. I don't understand your question. What is the point?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's an example, isn't it, of state or republican institutions issuing instructions as to the structure and name of municipal-level civilian administration?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who signed this decision referred to Article 5, 6, and 7 of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch what the witness said. So the decision is based on previous regulations. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you repeat what you said?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the signatory of this document, of this decisions in the preamble referred to Articles 5, 6, and 7 of the constitutional law for the implementation of the constitution of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so in the preamble he refers to a legal basis so this is not an arbitrary decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. I'm not seeking the legal history or background of this document. It's not my purpose and I don't have the time for that. All I'm asking you is simply this: Legal or otherwise, okay? This is an example of the state, republican level institutions, the President of the Presidency, affecting the composition of municipal-level civilian administration?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're trying to get a principled idea that the state organs are interfering with municipal bodies. You're trying to get that across. If a republic body is based, grounded within the law, they can issue such decisions. This is well known. This is a well known method.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It gives instructions for the formation of War Presidencies and in Article 2 it gives instructions for the composition of War Presidencies, right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think in Article 2, it states who should be there, if I'm reading this correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Article 3, which we've already looked at, goes on to set out that the War Presidency shall do various things in relation to the defence of the people, and then in Article 4, you see that the Presidency can appoint a representative on the War Presidency. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that representative of the republican-level government can have quite an active role, they can undertake all measures relating to appointments, organisation of work and so on? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would like me now to draw conclusions which are outside of Article 4, but if you ask me how I interpret Article 4, I do it in the following way. The signatory, the person who reached this decision, included provisions in Article 4 so in places where the local authorities are not functioning, there are problems in constituting the local authorities, then this trustee would help in doing that. This is how I interpret that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was in fact a War Presidency formed in Bosanski Samac, was it not? Was there not? And Dr. Blagoje Simic was president of that War Presidency? If you want, I can show you the document.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not disputing that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go back to Article 4. Article 4 in the second sentence or paragraph of Article 4, it very clearly says that the republican representative has got to ensure, amongst other things, ensure permanent coordination and implementation of the policies and measures defined and adopted by the republic's state institutions. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm reading that text in the same way that you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we are reading this text. I still don't understand what you're trying to get, what is the point? What is it that I should be explaining in Article 4, paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nothing. I'm just drawing your attention to that particular requirement, that the republican representative ensure permanent coordination and implementation of policies and measures adopted by the republic's state institutions.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you permit me, I would like to comment. You are trying to prove here that there was subordination and coordination from the level of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina down to the municipal level and that the Crisis Staffs were the key bodies. I would like to say that that wasn't so. The Crisis Staffs often were just a form, and that substantially the power was held by the army. They are the ones who had the power. You are trying to say the whole time that the centre of all events was the Crisis Staff and that is not so. And that is my general assessment regarding all of these events that happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you for to you comment on your assessment of what I am driving at, okay? I'm just asking you to note the plain words, the plain, simple words, the plain printed words, that appear on -- in Article 4, and the plain, printed words are: The republic will appoint a representative to work with the War Presidency and ensure permanent coordination and implementation of the policies and measures defined and adopted by the republic's state institutions. Now, that's clear and plain as day, isn't it? You couldn't get -- you couldn't get more clearer words, could you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read it the same way that you can read it, and we can agree on that, if we read the same text twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the national assembly is a state institution, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the national assembly adopts various strategic objectives, they must surely be policies or measures adopted by a state institution?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not questioning the authority of the bodies of the state institutions. They are well known, according to the constitution, the constitutional laws and other regulations. This is an axiom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can the witness be shown P5, please? And may I see it as well, the actual exhibit itself, before it's handed to the witness, please? Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment? Thank you. Would you look at paragraph 386?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a decision on the strategic objectives of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it has at the end of that decision the name of Momcilo Krajisnik, President of the national assembly and it has six strategic objectives listed there, does it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that here in the text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would agree with me that a decision on something called the strategic objectives of the Serbian people can only be described as a policy?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is certain that the assembly intended to establish the strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm not asking you about the motives or what was in their mind. It's a very, very simple matter, really simple. If you have before you a document that says, "This is a decision on the strategic objectives of the Serbian people," then it can only be described as a policy of a state institution, can't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it is over-ambitious to claim that it was totally the official policy but it was certainly a part of the policy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, one of the features of this policy is the establishment of state borders separating the Serbian people from the other two ethnic communities, and that's obviously a reference to Muslims and Croats, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to go back to Dayton once again, because Dayton verified this, what happened with the falling apart of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect Mr. Ninkovic, I'm not asking you about Dayton. All I'm asking you is, is what is there in plain black and white part of this policy is the establishment of state borders separating Serbs from the other two ethnic communities and those other two ethnic communities can only be in the context of the circumstances of this case, and the times and so on, they can only be Croats and Muslims, right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is impossible to explain this decision, if we mention the word strategic then you cannot look at things in an isolated way, outside of the general contexts. If a strategic project is planned, it's planned on the basis of general strategic events, the situation and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just go back for a third time. The reference to establishing state borders separating the Serbian people from the other two ethnic communities, the reference to the other two ethnic communities can only as a matter of reasonable logic, that can only be a reference to Croats and Muslims, right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but I don't see that from this text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other two ethnic communities were there? There were only three, they are the Serbs and Croats and Muslims or Bosniaks, right? We all know that. You surely don't deny that, do you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in a place like Bosanski Samac --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, just for the sake of clarity, the answer "yes" does that mean Mr. Ninkovic is denying or agreeing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am just stating here the position that the other two ethnic communities are Muslims and Croats. The dominant ones, besides the Serbs. And this is what I meant when I said yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But your attempts to prove that this is a strategic document, without taking into account the position that the general strategic atmosphere, without taking that into account, is a very narrow approach and it's not objective. Your approach is not objective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your time is complete, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Just a few more minutes, if Your Honours please this is my last topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have to finish this witness today and Mr. Pantelic said he needed about 30 to 40 minutes for re-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, can I just ask one or two more questions, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah, finally. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Establishing state borders separating Serbian people from other two ethnic communities, that's going to be very difficult, isn't it, in a place like Bosanski Samac where Croats and Muslims and Serbs live cheek by jowl, where they are all living together. That's going to be very hard, isn't it, to carry out that sort of programme?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you said, about an hour ago, there were ethnically pure settlements of Serbs and Croats in the territory of the municipality of Samac, as you said, so there were purely Serb villages and purely Croat villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, the last question, item number 1 of that decision is really a recipe for what later became known as ethnic cleansing and that is in fact what took place in the municipality, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot agree with you at all on that point. It's a very pretentious formulation which I cannot extrapolate from this first decision, and I see from what you say also that you are not objective in your approach to these charges. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Usher, please, could you just leave this exhibit because I'm going to examine on it. Your Honour when I said that I would need between 30 and 40 minutes, that was in the more or less in the at the midway of the examination of my learned friend. So I have some other exhibits now and topics so I kindly ask not to be very strict to this time limit. I'll do my best to organise my questions within this time limit but when I said 30 and 40 minutes that was let's say one hour and a half ago when the other topics were not raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, just go ahead with your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm very mindful about time as usual. Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me just a few more questions, Mr. Ninkovic, with regard to this. Could you please just move this document that's on the ELMO so that I can see the date up there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has to be turned on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at what is on the ELMO. However could you just move the document a bit towards you? Right, excellent. Could you read in the upper right-hand corner what the date is? The upper right-hand corner of this document.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 26th of November, 1993. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I meant. Did you personally ever have any knowledge regarding this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about this decision and its contents ever being discussed by the local authorities in Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was never discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will -- I finished with this exhibit, thank you Mr. Usher. MR. DI FAZIO: Just for the purposes of the record I think we should be clear that the witness was talking of P5 and that's what the question related to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's the exhibit. MR. DI FAZIO: I just wanted to be absolutely clear about that. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm grateful to my friend for this intervention. Thank you. Yes, that was Exhibit P5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, in order to be efficient you talked about the municipality of Samac, the Serb Municipality of Samac, the pre-war municipality of Samac, in response to the questions put by my learned friend Mr. Di Fazio, there was an entire series of these questions. In order to clarify certain matters, and in order to assist the Trial Chamber in reaching their decision, I'm going to ask you to look at a map. Let's comment on that, please. [In English] 31/1, please. [Interpretation] As far as I can remember. While Madam Registrar is looking for this document, I want to ask you some other things. Right now you are president of the municipal assembly of Samac, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As such, as this kind of official, and in view of your long years of experience in administration, what can you say? You as president of the municipality, do you reach decisions of the municipal assembly or is this done in some other way?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statute of the municipal assembly defines -- MR. DI FAZIO: Apart from -- I can't quite understand the question but I'm -- one thing I can understand is that it doesn't arise out of cross-examination as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact -- MR. DI FAZIO: If it does, exactly, as Mr. Weiner points out to me, he's talking about events that are occurring --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: At present. MR. DI FAZIO: -- at the present time as well, so I just don't see how this clarifies anything that I raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I can understand. I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were answering the Prosecutor's questions, for example when certain enactment was passed and we'll go back to that, when an enactment adopted by the municipal assembly was published in the Official Gazette and then when the signature said Dr. Blagoje Simic as president of the municipal assembly, these are the kind of things I'm talking about, was it he personally who passed this decision or was a different process involved? Because the formulation of the question put to you by the Prosecutor was such that it went in that direction?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. These are internal matters related to the work of parliament assemblies, that is to say the chairing person, the President of the assembly, has only one vote. He only has his own vote. And every decision is passed by a majority vote out of all the assemblymen present and this is in line with the Statute of the assembly. However, the President of the assembly signs these documents because that is the way things are, according to protocol and he represents the assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please take a look at this map? If it's easier for you, just take a look at it directly at the ELMO. Could you please tell me the following? This red line, what could that be? The one that goes across the municipality?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean right of the red line?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you specifically about that red line. What is your interpretation, what is this red line that goes through the territory of the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This red line is the border between the entities on the basis of the Dayton Accords. That is to say that is the boundary between the Republika Srpska and the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And what is this thin black line that goes for example from the Sava River and then goes by Orasje, Gradacac, Modrica and then goes up to the Bosna, what is that line?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the boundary of the pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac. And the pre-war of -- municipality -- boundary of the pre-war municipality of Odzak. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please I think we have got a key or a legend or an index or whatever the right -- yes, a legend at the bottom left-hand corner that tells us what all these lines are. These questions aren't necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic? The map is self explanatory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, tell me the following now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You can take your seat because I will discuss this exhibit, several questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mr. Ninkovic, right now, or perhaps let me put the question this way. What is your personal knowledge as to the following: Since when has there been a municipality Domaljevac Samac if there has ever been one?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality of Domaljevac Samac has been in existence since the war days and it is in part of the territory of the pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac. Specifically it includes Domaljevac, Bazik, and Grebnice. These were local communes, settlements, within the pre-war municipality of Bosanski Samac. I can testify about the number of inhabitants specifically as well. Domaljevac had a population of 400. Bazik, 800, and Grebnice had a bit over 2.000. The municipality had 32.800 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you know, which MPs constitute the assembly of the municipality of Domaljevac Samac, I mean their ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are Croats and during the war, these were assemblymen who had been elected in 1990, which means that they constituted the municipality of Domaljevac-Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this municipality still exist?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any Serb MPs in that assembly?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any during the war? I mean from 1992 onwards?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but in the municipality, in the municipal assembly that I chair, there are both Croats and Muslims, there are their representatives among the authorities, whereas in Domaljevac there aren't any. And now after Dayton as well. That is a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Ninkovic, do you have any personal knowledge about the following? The civilian authorities in the Serb part of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, during 1992, and 1993, did they ever discuss the takeover of power in the territory of the municipality of Domaljevac Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, you can take this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Ninkovic, when you say -- sorry, Mr. Pantelic, when you asked the question, the civilian authorities in the Serb part of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, et cetera, can you be specific? You're referring to the Crisis Staff and so on? I think it would be useful to have the specific body named rather than the general.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Her Honour Judge Williams is right. I should clarify this. So my question pertained to the Crisis Staff, the War Presidency and the executive council as well as the municipal assembly of Samac, when I mentioned the civilian authorities. That's what I meant. So within these forums, in these institutions, was this ever discussed, practically the takeover of territory and of power of Domaljevac Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I immediately understood your question so I will repeat my answer. As far as I know, never was there any discussion at any one of these institutions or authorities concerning the takeover of Domaljevac Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you know, maybe you don't know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes, I was just going to add a supplementary question. You've been stating that you were not a member of the Crisis Staff and even though you were in the building where it met, you weren't at all of its meetings, so I'm just wondering how you would know what was discussed or not discussed on this issue, if you, as you say, were not a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you listen to me carefully, I said as far as I know, no. Perhaps one could have a look at the transcript and see that that is actually what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes, in fact that's what you did say but I wanted for the sake of the record to hear you address specifically with regard to your status of not being a member of the Crisis Staff, as you put it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question with regard to this subject. Did you ever hear in any contacts, informal conversations in town, when talking to your colleagues, your friends, with people who held certain offices, did you ever hear any mention of this subject that we have been discussing now?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to answer with a few words, because I think the leadership of the municipality of Samac had the ambition of defending the territory it held, not that there were any aspirations vis-a-vis the territories that were not under their control. So I never heard anywhere of anyone showing any aspirations in that sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let us go back to the period of April, 1992, April, May, 1992. My question is the following: Do you have any personal knowledge in terms of the following, that in April, 1992, in the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, specifically in the town of Samac, where the seat of the municipal assembly was, at the moment when the conflict broke out, did you see or did you know that assemblymen of the municipal assembly of Bosanski Samac who were ethnic Croats were there in town at the moment when the conflict broke out, did you know about them being in town? MR. DI FAZIO: A, the witness said he wasn't there, he said he was in Skarici, the village of Skarici. He wasn't there when the conflict broke out. He only turned out later, and B, it didn't arise in my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, please, in fact, the basis of my question was to introduce personal knowledge or to explore personal knowledge of this witness with regard to the exhibit P124, I believe, and specifically with regard to the deputies, the ethnic background of the deputies in this municipal assembly. So -- MR. DI FAZIO: The time for exploration is over. That was to occur if it was to occur at all in examination-in-chief. The purpose of re-examination is to clarify anything that I have wrongly left unclear and that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. MR. DI FAZIO: It doesn't go beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's exactly Your Honour what I would like to achieve in my redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The objection is sustained so can you proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you about whether in the Serb Municipality of Samac, in the assembly, whether there were Croat and Muslim assemblymen. He asked you about that this afternoon, remember that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is the following: I have to clarify this with you. I'm not talking about the specific date of the 16th or the 17th. I'm talking about the weeks following the second half of April and May. Did you see any assemblymen who were ethnic Croats in Samac at that time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge as to where these assemblymen were, these assemblymen headed by the President of the then municipal assembly, Mato Nujic? Also an ethnic Croat. Did you personally know where they were?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that, the municipality of Domaljevac-Bosanski Samac. They constituted the municipality of Domaljevac-Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have please Exhibit P125, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please place page 1 on the ELMO? My learned friend asked you today, Mr. Di Fazio, about Article 1 of the Statute, and I am now asking you the following: Do you have any personal knowledge about what the motive was of the Serb deputies in the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina in October, 1991, to leave that parliament? To leave that assembly?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a well-known matter. There was a violation of the constitution and the constitutional rights of Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your personal knowledge about what the Serb deputies, after they left the parliament, what did they establish?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They established the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was any territory planned that would form that republic? And if you know, what would that territory comprise?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, those would be the territories with the majority Serb population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about whether in the territory of the municipality of Samac, in early 1991, a plebiscite was held about the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the local plebiscite, if you remember. If not, it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, Mr. Lukic asked for permission to address the Trial Chamber. So maybe we can adjourn -- you complete your re-examination tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that Mr. Lukic can take up the matter he wants to address.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And can the witness be escorted out of the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Your Honours, today, when I came into the courtroom, I was very surprised, unpleasantly, when I saw that my client came to the courtroom on crutches, during the break I talked to him and he told me that he has an injured knee, luckily he told me it's not a serious injury. He had a blood vessel burst in his knee and he is under treatment. So he expects for the bandages to be taken off by Monday. But he authorised me, since the doctor told him that he should rest but he wanted to come and attend the cross-examination today, but since the doctor did suggest for him to rest for the next couple of days, and since the schedule plans all day hearings for the next two days, he has told me that he would like to spend the next couple of days in his cell in the detention unit, so -- and he agrees that the trial should continue without him, and if he needs to sign anything, he's willing to do so, but he expects next week when our presentation of the case begins that he would be quite well. Since I will talk with the warden tomorrow, I hope that I will be able to stay in touch with my client during the breaks in the proceedings tomorrow. I hope that will be made possible for me so that I could keep him up to date, and I think that it will be enough for me to stay in touch with him during the break so that he would stay up to date with the proceedings by telephone. So this is all that I wanted to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Lukic. Yes, it's very kind of Mr. Tadic to agree that the trial should proceed in his absence and that he will remain resting, tending his injury in the detention unit so we will proceed as scheduled and I'm sure that you will be able to make contact with your client during the breaks and apprise him or between the two of you, you can divide your labour, one can go after one session and brief the accused so that if he has any instructions to give that can be done so that should be divided between the two of you. We shall now adjourn and continue our proceedings tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 6.53 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of January, 2003, at 9:30 a.m. 25
